newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu says Arafat must curb terrorism "now".
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says Arafat must curb terrorism "now".

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday that the future of the Middle East peace process depends on whether Yasser Arafat decides "now" to crack down on militants to stop bloodshed by suicide bombers in Israel.

"We expect the Palestinian Authority to do what it hasn't done so far. That is, to make an all-out effort, an all-out sweep to round up the terrorists, the leaders and interrogate them," he said on the CBS-TV programme "Face the Nation."
He spoke from Jerusalem, where Israeli authorities were taking extra precautions against further strikes by Islamic militants after two suicide bombers killed 13 people there last week.

Police were on alert ahead of a demand that Israel free all Palestinian prisoners by 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Sunday. A leaflet claiming the attack on Wednesday in the name of the Islamic militant Hamas group made the demand.

"If the Palestinian Authority made a bold decision to move with the side of peace and with the side of the difficult but necessary and extremely important negotiations for peace with Israel, rather than curry favour with terrorist, they would have made the right choice ....
"The whole peace is at stake. Arafat must make a choice and must make it now," Netanyahu said.
Under the Oslo peace agreement Israel agreed to give the Palestinians territory in return for a pledge that Arafat "will fight terrorism from within," Netanyahu said.
Wednesday's attack at a Jerusalem market was the deadliest since Netanyahu won election in 1996 vowing to bolster security.

He could not say whether there was any connection between the bombing in Jerusalem and the suspects arrested last week in an alleged New York subway suicide bombing plot. New York authorities said there was a link between the suspects and a radical Palestinian group.

Appearing on the same programme, National Security Advisor Sandy Berger said the United States has not established any direct relationship between the New York suspects and the Middle East, though he said, "Obviously the individuals involved in the New York plot had Middle East connections."

He said that U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, who postponed a planned trip to Israel until after a mourning period for last week's bombing victims, will discuss Israel's security when he visits Israel.
